g.text: Restaurant Rush - class overview (members hidden; full detail in class-diagram)
GameController depends on the GameUI interface,
which lives in the control package. GameCLI (and
the scripted test doubles) implement it, so no game
rule lives in the console code and whole games run
Inheritance + one rule for every role
perform() runs an action only if the staff member
has not acted this turn, and uses up the task only
when the action succeeds - so a rejected choice can
be retried. Host and Waiter both seat through
Restaurant.seat(), so they can never disagree.
The controller never checks a customer's type.
dispatched to the subclass: VIP pays 10% less and
loses 5; Critic loses 12 and takes -20 for food
served more than one turn after it became READY.
Seating, ordering, serving and every status change are
package-private (~) and guarded by the object that owns
the state (requireStatus, canCook, canServe), so control
and boundary code cannot bypass a rule: they get public
queries and unmodifiable lists. The Order constructor is
create an order and lock its price:
A ComboMeal is a MenuItem built from two MenuItems
and delegates to them: prepUnits = sum of the parts,
price = 90% of their total. Order and Chef only see
MenuItem, so combos needed no change there. The parts
are shared with the menu (Salad is also sold alone),
so this is aggregation; Restaurant owns its Tables and
percentOff() rounds half-up to the cent.
Visibility: + public, - private, # protected, ~ package-private. Underlined = static, italic = abstract.
«record»: each component is a private final field with a public accessor of the same name.
Omitted: implicit default constructors, record accessors, equals/hashCode, StatusView's private formatting helpers, lambdas.
